drug_class: Anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody (a type of targeted biologic therapy)
purpose: Ofatumumab is used to treat certain types of multiple sclerosis (MS) and a type of blood cancer called chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). For MS, it helps reduce flare-ups and slow the disease from getting worse. For CLL, it helps fight cancer cells in people who have not responded well to other treatments.
how_it_works: Your immune system has certain white blood cells called B-cells, which can mistakenly attack your nerves in MS or grow out of control in CLL. Ofatumumab works like a smart guided missile — it attaches to a protein called CD20 found on the surface of these B-cells and destroys them. By reducing these harmful B-cells, it helps calm the immune attack or fight the cancer.
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions (redness, swelling, or pain where the shot is given), upper respiratory infections like colds, headache, tiredness, nausea, and low white blood cell counts which can raise your infection risk.
warnings: This medication can seriously lower your immune system, making it harder to fight infections, including serious or life-threatening ones. It may reactivate hepatitis B virus if you have had it before. Do not receive live vaccines while on this medication. Tell your doctor immediately if you develop signs of infection such as fever, chills, or unusual tiredness. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should talk to their doctor before using this medication.
typical_dosing: For MS (Kesimpta): The starting doses are given as injections under the skin once a week for the first three weeks, then once a month after that. For CLL (Arzerra): It is given as an IV infusion in a clinic, with doses and timing determined by your doctor based on your specific treatment plan. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
